NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
F134.2 shrunk the discard charter to two requirements: fold inside the verb, and document that supersede discards governance never code. Those two still stand. The range-close that makes fold possible is no longer a borrowed terminal. D21 ruled that if the operation cannot be represented truthfully without breaking the skill rule that forbids the binary from emitting terminal, the schema gives way, not the rule. A discarded kind meaning abandoned is therefore in scope, on a different and stronger ground than the legibility argument F134.2 correctly rejected.
Rename already preserves run/. The HEAD probe archived run/1-T-001-opened.xml. The defect is not that files vanish on renameSync; it is that the durable instrument (Epoch, attempts, status.epochCount) is not written. C-SUPERSEDE-VERB's absent run/ is a revert artifact, not proof that supersede deletes loose events. Folding before the move is still required: archive measurements read Epoch-N, not leftover run/ files.
The brief's "exit 0, silently" for unterminated fold is false at this HEAD: exit 1, stderr "unterminated range for w0". F131's "exited 0" for the no-events message is also false today (C-PHASE-RULE-PIN and C-SUPERSEDE-VERB both exit 1). The spec uses the measured refuse, not the brief's recollection.

Alternatives.Alternative: Fold only in the CLI handler (src/grace-supersede.ts:72-95). Leaves supersedeChangeBundle as a write+rename helper. The EXDEV test would not fold, which is convenient, and the comment "Command-path only" would stay literally true. Rejected: F133. The product verb has two callers; a mechanism at the handler does not reach the function the tests and any future caller use. The CLI already only delegates.

Auto-emit kind=terminal from supersede (the draft's first design). Satisfies fold and grammar without a new kind. Rejected by D21: emitting terminal is a completion judgment the binary must not derive. F134.2 remains correct that no surface claims the work completed; that is not enough once the binary itself writes the lie.

Relax fold's terminal check when the caller is supersede, and fold an unterminated range. Avoids a new kind. Rejected: grammar validates the written Epoch with the same terminal requirement (ledger.range-unterminated). Fold must not be relaxed. D21's third option — a kind meaning abandoned — is the one that keeps both invariants and the skill rule.

Map discarded to CursorState complete. No new state. cursor show would print State: complete for an abandoned bundle, which F134.2 tolerated as a nit when it was inherited from terminal. Rejected: KNOWN_KIND_STATE would then assert the completion D21 forbids. A new state discarded is cheap (complete itself has three definitional non-test sites in grace-cursor.ts).
Document only in ngrace-cli. Rejected: ngrace-cli's shape_sources says the live inventory is the README table bound to listLiveInvocations, and forbids restating it there.

Skip skill-text edits and change only meta.description and README. Smaller blast radius (no token-accounting pin). Rejected for the agent readers: plan and execute are the surfaces that tell an agent to run the verb. --help is not. F133 still applies: a skill edit forces the byte pin, so those files are named in the spec rather than discovered at execution. The kind marker is additionally required by the completeness test at src/grace-cursor.test.ts:3213.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Effort accounting. The bundle after that.

Scenarios.Scenario: Abandoned mid-execution, open epoch, no range-closer. supersede emits discarded on the last task, folds, archives. Ledger holds the attempts. Replacement keeps the code. No terminal event is added by the verb.
Never executed, spec-only, no run/. supersede skips fold, writes superseded, archives. Same as today, exit 0.
Already folded, empty run/, still active (EXDEV retry). Skip fold, write, rename.
Already terminated but not folded. Skip the extra discarded, fold, archive.
recover --fix on an open epoch with no range-closer. Still emits only a covering opened. Fold remains blocked until the operator emits terminal or supersede emits discarded.
